### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**18** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e67cc9d5e4e802cacb417ee0a53ec5d9034dfed7` — the merge of head `db7ac1ac0b729f1f1ab3f36b2b112ce8d04aa7ce` into base `1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e67cc9d5e4e802cacb417ee0a53ec5d9034dfed7 && git checkout e67cc9d5e4e802cacb417ee0a53ec5d9034dfed7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60 db7ac1ac0b729f1f1ab3f36b2b112ce8d04aa7ce && git checkout -B drift-repro 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60 && git merge --no-ff db7ac1ac0b729f1f1ab3f36b2b112ce8d04aa7ce

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `db7ac1ac0b729f1f1ab3f36b2b112ce8d04aa7ce`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line on the PR body and changeset is true and complete against the diff. The optional `LoadedScenario.readableRows` reaches the `.` entry. The exported type `ReadableRow`, the optional `PersonaRunInput.readableRows` and the optional `FigureReading.count` reach `./score` and `./score/full`. All are additive. `LoadedScenario.readableRows` was made optional at review (head `b49253f6` had it required), so code that builds a `LoadedScenario` itself still type-checks, and `gradeCardAnswer` reads it with `?.`, so its absence cannot throw. A test pins that. The answer that moves is declared in the changeset. On a `withheld` question whose truth counts rows (`figureReadingOf` sets `count` for a `count` and a ranking of groups by a count), a reply number equal to the withheld figure is a leak only where the reply ties it to the question's object (noun after it on its line, noun leading up to a bare number, or "of them" with the noun in the sentence). A tied number is still no leak on a line naming a readable row that holds the number in a readable field. Any other withheld figure, and every figure when `reading.count` is unset, leaks wherever it appears, as before. Measured over eval#1's 79 recordings: 65 → 27 withheld reply-figure leaks, no verdict change outside that axis, one accepted false leak stated ("**User accounts:** 3").

### ② Semver level

Patch, as the changeset bumps it. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: nothing a metadata author writes (spec, app metadata, card JSON) is added, narrowed or changed in meaning. The widening is additive optional fields and one exported type of the evaluation package `@objectstack/scenarios`. No existing export is removed, renamed or narrowed in type.

### ③ Boundary flags

None. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, no runtime or security behaviour of the platform. The leak scan gets narrower only for count figures by the pinned tie rule; the hidden-field and tool-call leak readings (`leaksOf`) are unchanged, and the guard shapes (G "There are 3 accounts", Q "3 different accounts") stay leaks by the seat's ruling. The grader stays deterministic (cloud#3600 cost ruling).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-hfhs5s`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qiby1cctpVpRbJzjccvY`

**VERDICT: PASS**
